Two deposit sources tie each code to its item, 4/4 and in agreement: gstyping.dta variable labels (Teacher Survey - authority / - strict / - discipline / -  warmth as effective learning) and readme.pdf, which keys an abbreviated English statement to each variable name. Words: the paper appendix Questions Used for Constructing Teaching Styles, block Warm vs. Distanced, items 16-19, in the Essex author-accepted manuscript (pp.53-54); identical wording in the HCEO working-paper version. Appendix order 16-19 matches ts_warmth_1-4 by content (authority/strict/discipline/warm). Curly apostrophe in item 1 (students’) rendered ASCII; otherwise verbatim. REStat PDF at direct.mit.edu is bot-walled and was not read. ANCHORS / DIRECTION, per item: the readme states Scale: 1-strongly agree 4-strongly disagree for all four ts_warmth items (opposite to the ts_ext_1-3 and ts_gender teacher items). For ts_warmth_1-3 (distanced-worded) that is shipped as-is: 1=I strongly agree..4=I strongly disagree, so high = warm. ts_warmth_4 is different: the readme restates it in the REVERSED sense (relationship based on respect, a quiet classroom environment is more important for effective learning than a warm teacher-student relationship ...) with 1=strongly agree, whereas the appendix (and the dta label warmth as effective learning) word it warm-first. Shipping the appendix wording therefore requires flipping the anchors: ts_warmth_4 option_text runs 1=I strongly disagree..4=I strongly agree with the warm statement. Both readings put high = warm on all four items, which is what 1_measures.do requires (egen warmth = rowtotal(ts_warmth_1-ts_warmth_4), no reversal, labelled Teacher Warmth / Warm Approach). Data corroboration (N=145 teachers, live table): all 6 inter-item r positive (0.19-0.51; ts_warmth_4 r=+0.19/+0.51/+0.42 with items 1/2/3), which rules out ts_warmth_4 being keyed opposite to 1-3; each item correlates negatively with the teacher traditional gender-beliefs sum (ts_gender_1-9, high=traditional, direction corroborated in batch_346): -0.095/-0.279/-0.293/-0.195, sum-score r=-0.29, matching the paper Table 1 sign for Warm Approach (-0.084) on the standardized gender stereotype score. The absolute direction of the whole block rests on the readme; the data pin that all four share it and that it is the warm-high direction the paper uses. Label strings are the main text quoted scale I strongly agree / I agree / I disagree / I strongly disagree; the appendix lists the same 4-point scale as completely agree, agree, disagree, completely disagree; middle points assigned by that stated monotone order. Data note: ts_warmth_4 is sharply bimodal (resp 1/2/3/4 = 27/4/2/112) against unimodal items 1-3 (e.g. 8/42/70/25); consistent with the long double-barrelled comparative wording, not corrected. Language: teachers in Turkish state primary schools; no Turkish wording in the deposit (readme.pdf, gstyping.dta variable/value labels, 1_measures.do, 2_tables.do) or the Essex/HCEO manuscripts, so the authors own English rendering ships; language=Turkish inferred from setting. No instructions published; left blank. Rights: paper footnote 10 says some teaching-style questions were adapted from the OECD TALIS 2013 questionnaire and others constructed by the authors, without saying which; these four were not checked item-by-item against TALIS and no restriction on them was located; study CC0 deposit; rests on silence, not a positive grant.
public_note: The teacher survey was administered in Turkish; the wording here is the authors own English rendering from the paper appendix, and item ts_warmth_4 is worded in the opposite direction to items 1-3, so its anchors run 1 = strongly disagree to 4 = strongly agree while items 1-3 run 1 = strongly agree to 4 = strongly disagree (higher = warmer on all four).
